competitive_position.claim: The company operates in a highly competitive New York City real estate environment where competitors may accept lower returns, and it faces risks from work-from-home trends and AI-driven changes in office space utilization.
quotes: We operate in a highly competitive environment located in New York City. We compete with a large number of real estate investors, property owners and developers, some of whom may be willing to accept lower returns on their investments.

Work from home, flexible or hybrid work schedules, open workplaces, videoconferencing, and teleconferencing have become more common in recent years. Changes in tenant space utilization, including from the continuation of work from home and flexible work arrangement policies, may cause office tenants to reassess their long-term physical space needs, which could have an adverse effect on our business.

We may become subject to costs, taxes or penalties, or increases therein, associated with natural resource or energy usage, such as a "carbon tax" and by local legislation such as New York City's Local Law 97, which sets limits on carbon emissions in our buildings and imposes penalties if we exceed those limits, and New York City's Intro 2317, or the "gas ban" bill, which limits any onsite fossil fuel combustion in new construction and major renovations.

competitive_position.claim: The company carries $300,000,000 per-occurrence general liability insurance and $1.7 billion per-occurrence all-risk property and terrorism insurance, but acknowledges it is ultimately responsible for any loss incurred by its captive insurer FNSIC on NBCR acts.

risks.basis: Stated directly in P4 and P1 as a material risk; the 55% revenue concentration is a reported figure.
risks.claim: Bloomberg L.P. accounts for approximately 55% of rental revenues in the nine months ended September 30, 2026, and loss of Bloomberg as a tenant or deterioration in its credit quality would adversely affect the company's results of operations and financial condition.
quotes: Bloomberg L.P. ("Bloomberg") leases approximately 952,000 square feet at our 731 Lexington Avenue property and accounted for revenue of $99,004,000 and $96,655,000 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively, representing approximately 55% and 60% of our rental revenues in each period, respectively.
If we were to lose Bloomberg as a tenant, or if Bloomberg were to be unable to fulfill its obligations under its lease, it would adversely affect our results of operations and financial condition.

risks.basis: Stated directly in P2 as a named risk factor with specific revenue figures.
risks.claim: 731 Lexington Avenue accounted for approximately 67% of rental revenues in 2025, and loss of or damage to the building in excess of insurance coverage would adversely affect the company's financial condition and results of operations.
quotes: 731 Lexington Avenue accounted for revenue of $143,534,000, $153,298,000 and $148,806,000 in the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively, representing approximately 67%, 68% and 66% of our rental revenues in each year, respectively.
Loss of or damage to the building in excess of our insurance coverage, including as a result of a terrorist attack, would adversely affect our results of operations and financial condition.

risks.basis: Stated directly in P2 as a risk factor; the AI reference is a forward-looking concern without quantified impact.
risks.claim: Work from home, flexible work arrangements, and the increased use of artificial intelligence may cause office tenants to reassess their long-term physical space needs, which could adversely affect the company's business.
quotes: Work from home, flexible or hybrid work schedules, open workplaces, videoconferencing, and teleconferencing have become more common in recent years. Changes in tenant space utilization, including from the continuation of work from home and flexible work arrangement policies, may cause office tenants to reassess their long-term physical space needs, which could have an adverse effect on our business.
Additionally, the increased use of artificial intelligence ("AI") could result in changes in tenant space utilization, including the need to reduce or reconfigure space.

risks.basis: Stated directly in P4 MD&A; the lease modification and termination are reported events with specific dollar amounts.
risks.claim: Kohl's terminated its 135,000 square foot lease at the Rego Park shopping center on August 2, 2026, and while a 15-year lease with Target was signed in June 2026, the company's retail anchor tenant base has changed, creating near-term transition risk.
quotes: On June 26, 2026, we entered into a lease modification agreement with Kohl's for its 135,000 square foot store at our Rego Park shopping center providing options for us and Kohl's to early terminate the lease in August 2026, subject to a termination payment of approximately $29,000,000 from Kohl's. Simultaneously, we entered into a 15-year lease, plus renewal options, with Target for that space.
On August 2, 2026, Kohl's terminated its lease and paid the remaining $25,100,000 of the $29,000,000 termination payment.

risks.basis: Stated in P3 risk factors and MD&A; the balance sheet figure is from F1. The maturity schedule is from P3.
risks.claim: The company carries $837,164 (table in thousands) in net mortgages payable as of September 30, 2026, including a $94,000 (table in thousands) loan on the Alexander apartment tower maturing November 1, 2027, and refinancing may not be available on acceptable terms.
quotes: As of December 31, 2025, total mortgages payable, excluding deferred debt issuance costs, was $836,691,000, and our rate of total debt to total enterprise value was 46%.
If we are unable to obtain debt financing or refinance existing indebtedness upon maturity, our financial condition and results of operations would likely be adversely affected.

risks.basis: Stated directly in P2 as a risk factor; the court order compelling DEC to finalize CLCPA regulations is referenced but the specific penalty amounts for Alexander's buildings are not quantified in the evidence.
risks.claim: New York State's CLCPA, New York City's Local Law 97 carbon emission limits, and the Intro 2317 gas ban could result in substantial compliance, energy, retrofit, and construction costs for the company's buildings.
quotes: We may become subject to costs, taxes or penalties, or increases therein, associated with natural resource or energy usage, such as a "carbon tax" and by local legislation such as New York City's Local Law 97, which sets limits on carbon emissions in our buildings and imposes penalties if we exceed those limits, and New York City's Intro 2317, or the "gas ban" bill, which limits any onsite fossil fuel combustion in new construction and major renovations.

Although these laws and regulations have not had any material adverse effects on our business to date, they could result in substantial costs, including compliance costs, increased energy costs, retrofit costs and construction costs.

risks.basis: Stated in P1 (10-K) and P4 (10-Q MD&A); the ongoing revenue shortfall is a reported comparative figure.
risks.claim: Home Depot's 83,000 square foot retail lease at 731 Lexington Avenue expired on January 31, 2025, and the company reported lower rental revenue from retail tenant expirations at that property in 2026, indicating the space has not been fully re-let at prior rent levels.
quotes: On January 31, 2025, Home Depot's 83,000 square foot lease at the retail portion of our 731 Lexington Avenue property expired. Annual rental revenues from Home Depot were approximately $15,000,000.

This was primarily due to (i) $18,800,000 of higher straight-line revenue resulting from Kohl's lease modification at the Rego Park shopping center and (ii) $1,142,000 of higher operating expense recoveries from higher operating expenses, partially offset by (iii) $1,039,000 of lower rental revenue from retail tenant expirations at 731 Lexington Avenue.
